Master alloys of Zr56.7Al13Ni5Cu26.3 (ZANC) were fabricated by arc melting in a water-cooled copper crucible under the Ti-gettered argon (Ar) atmosphere.
The cylindrical rods of their alloys with a diameter of 2 mm and a length of 50 mm were produced by arc melting and suction casting into a water-cooled copper mold.
The alloys were heated to their Tg temperature based on the results of thermal properties at a heating rate 5 K/min and held for 30 min at a vacuum pressure of 1.3 × 10−5 torr.
The samples, then, were reheated to peak temperatures from 673 to 1073 K at a heating rate 5 K/min and held for 30 min in a vacuum chamber. After heat treatment, all samples were cooled in furnace.

evidence.quote: The Zr-based bulk amorphous alloys contained nano-sized crystalline particles showed excellent mechanical properties of compressive fracture strength over 2.0 GPa and compressive plastic strain of approximately 1%.
the Zr2Cu particles as well as complex crystalline particles are consist in the heat-treated alloy, which lead to the brittle fracture and the alloy show the low strength of 605 MPa.
It was confirmed that the dispersed crystalline particles act as reinforcing phases, which leads to an increase in the strength of the amorphous alloys.
